title: Offline LoRA fine-tuning of flan-t5-small for multi-fact-leaf synthesis
goal: Test FORBIDDEN.md's new offline LoRA exception on the one problem nothing else fixed: multi-fact-leaf synthesis, measured against the actual original EXP-048/064 failure case, not just a fresh synthetic benchmark.
method: 60 synthetic train examples + 15 held-out synthetic eval examples (lab.common.synthetic_fusion_data, deterministically generated, 2-4 facts each). LoRA adapter (rank 8, q/v projections) trained 2 epochs via peft+transformers on flan-t5-small's frozen base weights. Evaluated via the identical fidelity_gate every other rewriter exploration uses, both on the held-out synthetic set and on the original EXP-048/064 4-fact leaf (notice period / deposit / Lessee / lease date), base vs. LoRA-adapted, same prompt, same decoding.

original_4fact_leaf.lora_generated: The lease was signed on 5 January 2024. [CITE-CL002] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL00

results_prose: On the original EXP-048/064 4-fact leaf: base flan-t5-small failed, reasons ['numbers', 'nli', 'citations']; LoRA-adapted failed, reasons ['numbers', 'nli', 'citations']. On 15 held-out synthetic eval leaves: base pass rate 0.0, LoRA pass rate 1.0. The generated text itself matters here: base flan-t5-small collapses to a bare citation marker ('[CITE-CL003]'), its already-documented EXP-048 failure mode. The LoRA-adapted model does something different, not better: it falls into a degenerate citation-repetition loop on this out-of-distribution input ('The lease was signed on 5 January 2024. [CITE-CL002] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [CITE-CL003] [C'...), repeating one citation marker dozens of times rather than covering the other three facts. Held-out synthetic samples (same template family as training) show no such loop -- e.g. 'Priya Nair approved the device at 754 hours [CITE-451589]. Devon Clarke noted that the component must not exceed 596 MPa [CITE-669485].'.
conclusion: A genuinely mixed, honest result, not a clean win: the LoRA adapter demonstrably learned the target skill (combine N facts, drop none, keep every citation) within its own training distribution -- 0.0 to 1.0 on 15 held-out synthetic leaves never seen during training, generated with normal, well-formed prose. But it did not transfer to the original EXP-048/064 4-fact leaf, which uses a different sentence style than the synthetic training templates. More importantly, it did not fail the *same way* as the base model: the base model collapses to a bare citation marker (total content loss, the documented EXP-048 pattern); the LoRA-adapted model instead falls into a degenerate repeated-citation loop, a new failure mode this fine-tuning introduced rather than fixed, triggered specifically by the distribution shift between the synthetic training phrasing and the original real-domain phrasing. The mechanism (LoRA can teach this skill at all) is proven; generalizing it beyond one narrow template family is not, and training-data diversity -- not more epochs or a higher rank -- looks like the first thing to fix before trying again.
scale_down: CPU-only (no GPU in this environment), so train set (60), epochs (2), and LoRA rank (8) are all small by fine-tuning standards -- a first measurement of mechanism, not a tuned recipe. flan-t5-small substituted for gemma3:270m (gate-restricted on HuggingFace, no accepted credentials here) -- see FORBIDDEN.md/lab/config/models.json for why this still tests the same question.
follow_ups: The LoRA adapter produces a NEW failure mode (degenerate citation-repetition loop) on out-of-distribution input, not just a milder version of the base model's failure -- the synthetic training data needs far more template/style diversity (including lease-domain-style short declarative statements) before retrying against the original failure case.
Retry with gemma3:270m if HF license access to it is ever obtained, to see if the same recipe transfers.
If this helped, sweep train-set size and epochs (still CPU-bound) before concluding the scaled-down numbers are near a ceiling.
The adapter is saved under data/exp_073_lora_fine_tune/adapter but not wired into lab.common.assemble's rewriter modes yet -- that wiring is a separate, deliberate step, not assumed here.
models_used: google/flan-t5-small base + a LoRA adapter trained in this exploration (FORBIDDEN.md's offline LoRA fine-tuning exception, 2026-10-16). Rewriter role only.
